title: About

title: Custom Instrumentation for Chiroptical Spectroscopy
content: A 3D-printed sample fixture for the CD spectrometer, designed in Fusion 360, and the chiral metasurface signal it made reproducible. The sample seat in the beam with and without the fixture, and the measured CD couplet at two sample positions.Shadi Mirmohammadi, Tang Lab, University of UtahProblem: sample placementCircular dichroism (CD) measures the difference in absorption between left- and right-circularly polarized light. For a chiral metasurface the signal is a few millidegrees riding on a much larger absorbance, so the position of the substrate in the beam matters: hand-placing a coated fused-silica chip in the sample compartment shifts and reshapes the spectrum from scan to scan.Fixture designI designed a two-part fixture in Fusion 360 and 3D-printed it. A rail mount slides into the Jasco spectrometer’s sample compartment at a fixed position along the beam path, and a square substrate holder, with a recessed pocket and corner mounting holes, seats the chip at the same position and orientation every time. The holder took six design iterations. The two Fusion 360 parts: (a) the rail mount that fixes the position along the beam path; (b) the square substrate holder, v6, with a recessed pocket and mounting holes.Result: a reproducible bisignate CD signalWith the fixture in place, the diarylethene (DAE) chiral metasurface shows a bisignate CD couplet across ~580–615 nm: a negative lobe reaching −10.5 mdeg near 580 nm and a positive lobe of +14.3 mdeg near 610 nm, several times above the ~1 mdeg (1σ) noise floor measured on air and bare fused-silica references. title: Electrochemical Sol-Gelation of CdS Quantum Dots
content: Growing 3D quantum-dot gel networks under applied potential: phase- and size-dependent electrogelation of CdS QDs. Quantum dots linking into a gel at the anode as the potential passes 1.7 V, the UV-Vis spectrum of the TGA-capped dots, and the SAXS power law with Df = 1.86. Gels grown by applied voltage Zinc-blende CdS quantum dots assembling into a three-dimensional network at the electrode, at 1.8 V. Your browser does not support the video tag. 1.8 V vs. Ag/AgCl · 36 µM CdS@TGA in methanol · gel nucleating on the Pt anodeShadi Mirmohammadi, Department of Chemistry, University of Utah, with the Luo lab; SAXS at the Utah Nanofab with Randy PolsonBackgroundIsolated quantum dots wrapped in insulating ligands are hard to wire into anything macroscopic. Gelation cross-links the dots into a continuous, porous 3D network that keeps quantum confinement while allowing electronic communication. Most QD gels are made by adding a chemical oxidant, which leaves residue and gives uncontrolled nucleation. This project uses electrochemistry instead: anodic oxidation of surface thiolates forms S₂²⁻ bridges between particles, so the gel grows directly on the electrode, and the applied potential sets the oxidation strength, giving controlled kinetics without a chemical oxidant.Quantum dot synthesisZinc-blende CdS quantum dots are synthesized by hot injection, with size set by growth time and sulfur precursor amount. Batches range from 2.6 to 4.9 nm with narrow spectral linewidths (HWHM ≈ 12–13 nm), cross-checked by XRD and TEM. To make the dots gelable, their oleic-acid shell is excha...

title: Photon Upconversion in CdSe–Anthracene Hybrids
content: CdSe nanoplatelet–anthracene hybrids that convert two green photons into one violet photon, and how the position of one carboxylic acid on the anthracene sets the upconversion yield. The energy ladder from two 532 nm photons to one 410 nm photon, and the measured upconversion yields of the three anthracene isomers.Seyedeh Shadi Mirmohammadi, Farwa Awan, Tsumugi Miyashita, Todd D. Krauss, and Ming Lee TangUniversity of Utah & University of RochesterPoster presented at the 2nd International Symposium on Photochemistry & Functional Interfaces (ISPF2), New York, 2024.View the poster (PDF). The 532 nm beam lights the table green, but the cuvette glows blue: anti-Stokes emission from triplet–triplet annihilation.Photon upconversionPhoton upconversion combines two low-energy photons into one higher-energy photon through triplet–triplet annihilation (TTA). A CdSe nanoplatelet absorbs the 532 nm (2.34 eV) photons; a mediator covalently bound to its surface, here anthracenecarboxylic acid (ACA), accepts the triplet by Dexter transfer (TET1); and a free emitter in solution, 9,10-diphenylanthracene (DPA), collects it (TET2). When two DPA triplets meet, TTA promotes one to the singlet state, which emits at 410 nm (3.06 eV). In this work we replaced the Tang lab’s CdSe quantum dots with nanoplatelets.NanoplateletsCdSe nanoplatelets (NPLs) are quantum-confined only in their thickness, which is controlled to the atomic layer (5.5 monolayers). There is no size polydispersity to broaden the spectra, the enhanced exchange interactions favor the dark (triplet-like) exciton that driv...

title: EIT-Like Terahertz Metasurface: a Full-Wave Design Study
content: A published EIT terahertz metasurface reproduced and extended in Ansys HFSS, covering metal thickness relative to the skin depth, substrate selection, and a coupled-resonator fit to the full-wave data. The coupled C-arc and S-arc cell, the simulated transmission window with its 5.3 ps group delay, and the results of the aluminum-thickness, substrate and graphene sweeps.Shadi Mirmohammadi, ECE 6310 (Advanced Electromagnetic Fields), University of Utah, Spring 2026 ·read the report (PDF)Coupled resonators and the transparency windowElectromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) is a quantum-optics effect with a metamaterial counterpart. When two bright resonators are coupled so that their responses interfere destructively, a narrow transparency window opens between two absorption dips, with the steep phase dispersion that gives slow light. Zhang et al. (Optics Express, 2022) built one at terahertz frequencies: an aluminum C-arc + S-arc pair on polyimide, with a transparency window at 0.87 THz and a peak group delay of 5.5 ps.Two fabrication questionsI rebuilt that metasurface in Ansys HFSS and asked two questions the paper did not address. First, how thick the metal needs to be: at 1 THz the skin depth of aluminum is δs ≈ 84 nm, yet the paper deposits 200 nm. Second, whether polyimide is the right substrate: its THz loss tangent (0.05) is among the worst of the thin-film polymers, and Parylene-C and BCB have 10–17× lower loss at similar permittivity. I swept six aluminum thicknesses (50–500 nm) and four substrates, fit a coupled-resonator model to the baseline data, and ad...

title: 10 kV β-Ga₂O₃ Photoconductive Switches
content: Impurity-engineered Fe:β-Ga₂O₃ photoconductive semiconductor switches that switch 10 kV with a near-infrared laser. The Fe level inside the Ga₂O₃ bandgap that an 808 nm photon can reach, the 10 kV test circuit, and the measured photocurrent against laser power at 1, 5 and 10 kV.Hunter Ellis, Imteaz Rahaman, Afrouz Taherian, Seyedeh Shadi Mirmohammadi, Botong Li, Michael A. Scarpulla, Berardi Sensale-Rodriguez, and Kai FuDepartment of Electrical & Computer Engineering, University of UtahManuscript ready for submission (2026).Switching 10 kV with near-infrared lightPhotoconductive semiconductor switches (PCSSs) are optically triggered high-voltage switches. Ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) semiconductors such as β-Ga₂O₃ (Eg ≈ 4.8 eV) are ideal hosts because blocking voltage scales with critical field, but band-to-band absorption requires deep-ultraviolet light, and high-power, fast UV sources are scarce. Fe doping introduces deep acceptor states ~0.8 eV below the conduction band, so an ordinary 808 nm near-infrared laser can photoionize electrons from the Fe states into the conduction band while the material keeps its full high-voltage blocking capability. (The same Fe:β-Ga₂O₃ photoconductivity is used in my optically tunable THz metasurface.) Transition-metal impurity levels inside the 4.8 eV gap of β-Ga₂O₃. Fe (0.8 eV below the conduction band) is reachable with near-infrared photons; deeper levels (Ir, Ni, Cu) need higher-energy light.The device and the experimentThe switch is built on an Fe-doped β-Ga₂O₃ substrate (0.01% Fe, 650 µm thick) and encapsulated in high-thermal-c...

title: Excitation-Switchable Eu³⁺ Luminescence in GdScO₃
content: A nominally undoped crystal changes its emission color with the excitation wavelength, and its luminescence reports on substrate quality. Energy transfer from the Gd³⁺ lattice to trace Eu³⁺, the measured spectra switching from green to red as the excitation tunes from 236 to 270 nm, the 491/612 nm line ratio, and the annealing results.Seyedeh Shadi Mirmohammadi, Afrouz Taherian, Yunshan Wang, Diego P. Fernandez, Michael A. Scarpulla, Steve Blair, and Berardi Sensale-RodriguezUniversity of UtahManuscript in preparation for Optical Materials Express (2026).Visible emission from a nominally undoped substrateGdScO₃ is a perovskite substrate for epitaxial oxide films. We studied commercial, nominally undoped single crystals from two vendors (Stonylab (100) and CrysTec (110)); under deep-UV excitation they show bright, sharp visible emission. The emission comes from europium at the parts-per-million level, an unintentional trace impurity (1–2 ppm, roughly one Eu³⁺ ion per 10⁵–10⁶ Gd³⁺). The trace emits strongly because energy absorbed anywhere in the Gd³⁺ sublattice migrates to the Eu³⁺ sites.Emission color versus excitation wavelengthWith the tunable deep-UV source (third-harmonic generation of a Ti:sapphire laser) I built for my GeO₂ photodetector measurements, we swept the excitation from 236 to 270 nm. At short excitation wavelengths the emission is dominated by the Eu³⁺ ⁵D₂/⁵D₁ lines (491 nm and the 535–555 nm group). With the excitation tuned into the Gd³⁺ ⁶IJ absorption near 266 nm, the emission is almost pure red ⁵D₀ → ⁷F₁,₂ at 590 and 612 nm. Excitation-emission map; ...

title: UV Photoresponsivity of GeO₂ Photodetectors
content: Measuring the deep-UV spectral response of ultrawide-bandgap GeO₂ detectors with a tunable third-harmonic laser source, in collaboration with the Fu and Blair labs. The third-harmonic deep-UV source with the beam-area correction, and the measured responsivity of the GeO₂ detector across the solar-blind band.Shadi Mirmohammadi, with Imteaz Rahaman, Botong Li, and Afrouz Taherian (Dr. Kai Fu’s lab) and Prof. Steve Blair, Electrical & Computer Engineering, University of UtahMotivationGermanium dioxide (GeO₂) is an emerging ultrawide-bandgap semiconductor. The film used here, rutile r-GeO₂(111) grown by MOCVD on r-TiO₂(111), has an optical bandgap of ~5.31 eV, deep in the solar-blind UV where sunlight does not reach the ground. Dr. Kai Fu’s group fabricated metal–semiconductor–metal detectors on their GeO₂ films (interdigitated contacts, 250 × 300 µm active area), and the quantitative test is how the responsivity varies with wavelength across the band edge.Deep-UV source and measurementWe generated tunable light at ~233–280 nm by third-harmonic generation (THG) of a tunable Ti:sapphire laser in Prof. Blair’s lab, using my setup for UV-pumped photoluminescence realigned for this experiment, and I calibrated the power at each wavelength on a Thorlabs power meter with a UV extension. At each wavelength we recorded dual-sweep I–V curves from −10 to +10 V in the dark and under illumination and computed responsivity as (Iphoto − Idark) / Pincident. The UV beam is ~7 mm across and the detector is 250 × 300 µm, so the incident power is corrected by the beam-to-device area ratio....

title: Optical Constants of 3D-Printable Glass on Doped SiC
content: Spectroscopic ellipsometry of Glassomer films on doped silicon carbide, with Cauchy and oscillator modeling of Ψ and Δ and validation against literature optical constants. Shadi Mirmohammadi, Electrical & Computer Engineering, University of UtahBackgroundDesigning a photonic device around a material requires its refractive index, n and k, across the wavelengths of interest. Spectroscopic ellipsometry measures the polarization change on reflection as the angles Ψ and Δ; the optical constants come from fitting a physical model to them. This study measures Glassomer, a 3D-printable silica-nanopowder-filled composite debound and sintered into fused silica, on doped silicon carbide.CalibrationThe instrument rejected a bare doped SiC wafer as the calibration reference. A bare polished substrate sits near Δ ≈ 0°/180°, where the polarization barely changes on reflection, so the calibration regression is ill-conditioned. A thin thermal SiO₂ layer on silicon moves Δ away from those values, so the SiO₂/Si standard works. α-SiC is also uniaxially birefringent, which violates the calibration’s isotropic assumption.MeasurementsFive stacks were measured: Sample Structure Thickness 1 Glassomer on doped SiC 0.3865 mm 2 Glassomer on doped SiC 0.3823 mm 3 SiC / Glassomer / SiC sandwich 0.7418 mm 4 Bare doped SiC (reference) 0.3662 mm 5 Bare doped SiC (reference) 0.3696 mm Ψ and Δ were recorded from 250 to 2000 nm at 60°, 65°, 70°, and 75° incidence. title: Engineering Spin States in Si QD–Organic Hybrids
content: Time-resolved EPR shows that Si quantum dots transfer a fully spin-polarized triplet to covalently bound anthracene derivatives. {% include data-anim.liquid %}Mandefro Y. Teferi, Sanoop Mambully Somasundaran, Shadi Mirmohammadi, Ming Lee Tang, Jens Niklas, and Oleg G. PoluektovArgonne National Laboratory & Department of Chemistry, University of UtahPaper: “Spin-Polarized Anthracene Triplet States Sensitized by Si QDs Revealed by Time-Resolved EPR Spectroscopy”, Nano Letters (2026), doi: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.6c03633. Accepted September 10, 2026.Why TR-EPRSi quantum dot–molecule hybrids generate long-lived triplet excitons, but nearly everything known about their triplet energy transfer comes from optical measurements, which do not resolve spin: a photodetector cannot tell whether a triplet formed by spin–orbit intersystem crossing, charge recombination, or direct energy transfer. Time-resolved electron paramagnetic resonance (TR-EPR) can.The conjugatesThe conjugates pair 2.6 nm dodecane-capped Si QDs with three anthracene derivatives covalently bound through different bridges: 9-ethylanthracene (9EA, flexible single bond), 9-vinylanthracene (9VA, π-conjugated C=C linker), and the larger 9,10-bis(phenylethynyl)anthracene (BPEA). The Nano Letters paper covers 9EA and 9VA; BPEA is from the ESP-2025 poster. The 480 nm excitation is absorbed only by the QD, so any triplet on the molecule came from the dot. 480 nm light excites only the Si QD; its dark, triplet-like exciton populates the anthracene triplet sublevels T₊₁, T₀, T₋₁ by Dexter transfer.The triplet arrives spin-p...

title: Optically Tunable THz Metasurface Absorber
content: An optically tunable terahertz metasurface absorber on Fe-doped β-Ga₂O₃: HFSS design, measured photoconductivity, the ITO electrode process, and the first resonator array on the crystal. Poster at IRMMW-THz 2026. {% include data-anim.liquid %}Seyedeh Shadi Mirmohammadi, Steve Blair, and Berardi Sensale-RodriguezDepartment of Electrical & Computer Engineering, University of UtahPoster at the 51st International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz 2026), Salt Lake City: Monday, October 12, 2026, 17:30 to 19:00, Poster Session 1, Board 1. Poster (PDF). An earlier version was presented at the ASCENT Summer School on Semiconductor Science & Technology, University of Michigan, August 2026 (poster).AbstractWe present an optically tunable terahertz (THz) metasurface absorber based on Fe-doped β-Ga2O3, an ultrawide-bandgap semiconductor (Eg ≈ 4.8 eV). Despite this large bandgap, Fe acceptor states enable sub-bandgap photoexcitation at 808 nm, producing pump-power-dependent photoconductivity. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations for σ = 0 to 25 S/m show 82.2% absorption modulation and 95.0% reflected-power modulation at 300 GHz, establishing Fe:β-Ga2O3 as a promising platform for optically reconfigurable THz photonics.Device designA gold H-shaped resonator array on a 724 μm thick Fe:β-Ga2O3 substrate over a gold ground plane: P = 150 μm, a = 120 μm, w = 15 μm, g = 5 μm, Au 0.2 μm. The topology follows the split-ring design of [2], scaled for 300 GHz and simulated in ANSYS HFSS 2025 R2. Fig. 1. Unit cell and the Au/Fe:β-Ga2O3/Au cross-section....
